title: Colson Montgomery’s homer was 112 mph off the bat. This White Sox fan caught it barehanded
content:
If this Chicago White Sox fan hoped to catch a home run on his birthday Saturday night, he probably should have brought a glove. Instead, he made use of what he had — his bare left hand.

In the bottom of the first inning, White Sox shortstop Colson Montgomery launched a 372-foot homer into right field at 112.3 mph off the bat. The ball screamed toward a fan who had nothing to protect him.

It didn’t matter. He caught it anyway.

His face, mouth agape as he seemed to process his own reflexes. The fan, Joe — who didn’t share his last name — later spoke with Chicago Sports Network.

“I literally cannot (believe it),” he said in the interview. “It was pretty loud, just walking down the steps, and then just saw it coming.”

It was Joe’s birthday and his first game of the season. He and his friends watched the White Sox (74-68) jump out to a 3-0 lead, courtesy of Montgomery’s 31st homer of the season, before the Sox lost 6-4 in the second game of a three-game series against the Twins (68-74) in Chicago.

Joe hadn’t brought the equipment necessary to catch a home run. Instead, he carried with him something better: a birthday wish from his father.

“He said, ‘Happy birthday! Hope you enjoy the day. Have fun at the game. Hopefully, you can catch a ball,’” Joe said, recalling the text his father sent him. “I said, ‘I’ll try my best to catch a ball.’ And then, lo and behold.”

A former high school right fielder, Joe saw the ball tailing toward him near the foul pole and prepared himself. A glove would have been preferable for a baseball that started his way at more than 100 mph.

But he didn’t need one.

He caught it barehanded, looking every bit as stunned as everyone who saw it.
